At the start of the Shaosheng era, Lai Zhishao and Zhou Zhi accused Liu Zhi of overturning reforms and abandoning territory; he was stripped of office and made prefect of Huangzhou, then demoted again to Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments with nominal duty at the Southern Capital and residence enforced at Qizhou.
光祿卿 is the chief minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments

梁燾 is read Liang Tao

At the end of Yuanyou, when Lü Dafang had been made Acting Vice Minister and Han Zhongyan though dismissed still enjoyed Emperor Zhezong's favor, Wen Jifu claimed his late father had said "Sima Zhao" meant Liu Zhi, "powder" meant Wang Yansou for his pale face, and "kun" meant Liang Can, whose courtesy name Kuangzhi punned on "elder brother."

Because at the end of Yuanyou Wen Jifu owed his appointment as Acting Vice Minister to Lü Dafang, and because Han Zhongyan though dismissed still enjoyed Emperor Zhezong's favor, Wen Jifu claimed his late father had said "Sima Zhao" meant Liu Zhi, "powder" meant Wang Yansou for his pale face, and "kun" meant Liang Tao, whose courtesy name Kuangzhi punned on "elder brother."
梁燾 is Liang Tao; 德大防除權侍郎 means Jifu was grateful to Dafang for appointing him acting vice minister
